BREAKING: US new home sales jumped +14.2% MoM in October, to an annualized rate of 701,000 units, the highest since December 2025, crushing expectations of a -3.8% decline.

This marks the largest monthly increase since November 2025 and the 2nd-largest since August 2022.

It also marks a sharp recovery from the -9.7% MoM decline in September.

October's surge was driven by sales in the South, the nation's largest home-selling region, which soared +36.2% MoM, to an annualized rate of 515,000 units, the highest since March 2021.

At the same time, the median new home sale price fell -0.3% MoM and -3.2% YoY, to $391,300, the 2nd-lowest reading since July 2021.

Since the October 2022 peak, the median new home sale price has declined by $69,000, or -15.0%.

New home prices are falling sharply.

US M2 money supply is now $8.18 trillion above its 2019 pre-pandemic levels.

BREAKING: US oil prices have recorded 3 drawdowns of at least 20% so far in 2026, matching their 2nd-longest such streak since the 1980s.

2020 was the only year with a longer streak, at 4 such declines, while 1990, 1991, 1998, and 2022 each recorded 3.

Taking intraday prices into account, US oil prices have posted 4 drawdowns of at least 20% this year.

Furthermore, oil prices have seen 8 corrections of 10%+ so far in 2026, their longest such streak since 1986.

The same number of 10%+ drawdowns was posted in 1990, 2004, and 2009.

Year-to-date, oil prices are up +42%, on track for the largest annual gain since 2021.

US oil prices have rarely been this volatile.

Gold has rarely been this oversold:

Gold prices are trading -20% below their 200-day moving average, their largest negative deviation since June 2013.

This marks a sharp reversal from the +45% deviation above the 200-day moving average recorded in January, the largest since the 1970s.

This comes as gold prices have dropped -37% from their January intraday peak, their largest drawdown within a 12-month period since the early 1980s.

By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, gold prices also declined -20% below their 200-day moving average.

However, the largest such negative deviation was recorded in 1981, at -27%.

Gold is experiencing one of its most severe declines in history.

To put a finer point on the earnings vs valuation question, below I show the S&P 500 index with five different P/E ratios: the n12m estimate, the l12m actual, and three different 5-year CAPE ratios using trailing earnings, the n12m estimate, and the n24m estimate. Because earnings are cyclical, using only a l12m or n12m multiple at a cyclical inflection point can be misleading. A 5-year CAPE ratio provides a better sense of valuations, especially if we include forward estimates to make it less backward looking. Below we see that the 5-year n24m CAPE is now 22.8x, down 4 points from 26.8x.  For perspective, during the Rate Reset cycle of 2022 this multiple contracted 7.9 points from 25.8x to 17.9x, and during the 2025 Tariff Tantrum it reset 3.8 points from 25.6x to 21.8x. In other words, the current derating real, but perhaps not as significant as the 27% drawdown in the n12m P/E-multiple would suggest.

A lot of us became AI believers, ended up far less diversified than we probably should be, and are now praying for a recovery in the most crowded trade of all time, just as plenty of clouds have rolled into the sky. I am optimistic about this selloff proving short-lived from here, and bottoming in December, but everyone has different timeframes and different risk tolerance. Respect yours.
